problem: Let $F(x)={x}^{3}-x$ for $x\in [0,\pi ),$ and let $f(x)$ be the **even** extension of $F(x)$ to $x\in (-\pi ,\pi ).$ What is $f(x)$ for $x\in (-\pi ,0)?$

feedback.problem: Let $F(x)={x}^{3}+2\operatorname{cos}⁡x$ for $x\in [0,\pi ),$ and let $f(x)$ be the **even** extension of $F(x)$ to $x\in (-\pi ,\pi ).$ What is $f(x)$ for $x\in (-\pi ,0)?$
feedback.worked_solution:
If $F(x)$ is defined on $x\in [0,\pi ),$ the even extension of $F$ is the function $f$ such that

$$
f(x)={\begin{aligned}F(x), & x\in [0,\pi ), \\ F(-x), & x\in (-\pi ,0).\end{aligned}
$$

In our case, for $x\in (-\pi ,0),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =F(-x) \\  & =(-x)^{3}+2\operatorname{cos}⁡(-x) \\  & =-{x}^{3}+2\operatorname{cos}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$
